matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: An anchor-free design combined with SimOTA dynamic label assignment improves YOLO accuracy without anchor box hyperparameter tuning.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: YOLOX switches the YOLO detector to an anchor-free manner.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: YOLOX adopts a decoupled head that separates classification and regression branches, replacing the coupled head used in earlier YOLO versions.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: Replacing the YOLO head with a decoupled one greatly improves converging speed.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: YOLOX-L achieves around 50 AP on COCO at roughly 69 FPS on a Tesla V100, surpassing YOLOv5-L by about 1.8 AP at the same speed.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: YOLOX-L achieves 50.0% AP on COCO at a speed of 68.9 FPS on a Tesla V100.

unmatched_a.a_claim_text_normalized: Coupled detection heads in earlier YOLO versions create a conflict between classification and localization branches that slows convergence and limits accuracy.
